newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end almost flat in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end almost flat in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed almost flat in dull trading with losses seen across the board, except for blue chip shares, brokers said on Monday.
They said cautious investors clung to the sidelines for lack of positive factors. Rising interest rates and the dollar's appreciation against the Korean won dampened sentiment.
The composite stock index closed down 1.22 points to 740.93. Declining issues outpaced advancers 494 to 291, with only 27.8 million shares changing hands.
"The market continued to consolidate in thin trading volume," said Baek Jung-hyun of Samsung Securities.
Among the blue chips, Samsung Electronics gained 300 won to 68,800 and and Pohang Iron and Steel Co added 500 to 64,200.

Brokers said investors were somewhat disappointed as an anticipated announcement by creditor banks on the rescue of the Kia Group did not materialise. A meeting on Monday to deal with Kia's problems focused on support for subcontractors.
Kia Group shares ended mixed. Kia Motors shed 200 won to 12,100 and Kisan dropped 560 won to its daily limit low of 6,550, while Kia Steel climbed 30 won to 2,280.
Brokers said the national convention by the ruling New Korea Party to select its nominee for the presidential election in December had little impact on the market.
Former supreme court judge Lee Hoi-chang led a race for the presidential nominee but failed to secure the 50 percent of votes cast needed to win nomination, party officials said.
A second round of polls would be held later on Monday between Lee and and the runner-up, Governor Rhee In-je of Kyonggi Province which surrounds Seoul, they said.
Brokers said talk that the ruling party would announce government steps to boost the economy after the convention to gain popularity may continue to affect market for the time being.
Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds closed Monday morning at 12.13 percent against 11.87 percent July 14.
